title: Nanoscape: The Journal for Undergraduate Research in Nanoscience
description: Nanoscape: The Journal for Undergraduate Research in Nanoscience is an annual publication of original research conducted by undergraduates from around the county. The journal was launched in 2004 and was the first of its kind in the country. The journal disseminates the results of undergraduate research in the broad fields of nanoscience and nanotechnology. Nanoscape is an educational outreach project of the Northwestern University Nanoscale Science and Engineering Center (NSEC), which is part of the International Institute for Nanotechnology (IIN), both of which are under the direction of Professor Chad A. Mirkin. This work was supported primarily by the Nanoscale Science and Engineering Initiative of the National Science Foundation Under NSF award number EEC–0755375 AND EEC-0647560.

title: Directed Assembly of Nanoporous, Porphyrin-Based, Molecular-Square Thin Films
creator: SonBinh T. Nguyen
Richard W. Gurney
Craig P. Schwartz
description:
Several phosphonate-functionalized molecular
squares have been successfully synthesized,
and the fabrication of multilayer films
on both conductive and semiconducting
platforms has been demonstrated. These
films were grown using the well-documented
zirconium phosphonate multilayer method.
The layer-by-layer growth rate is uniform.
Experiments suggest, however, that the
molecular squares adopt a semi-collapsed
structure upon assembling in multilayer films.
Despite this structure, the films are still
impermeable to molecules larger than the
dimensions of an individual square cavity but
highly permeable to smaller species. This
research also has successfully observed a
single iteration of the zirconium phosphonate
multilayer assembly of the molecular square
by scanning electron microscopy and atomic
force microscopy through micromolding in
capillary micropatterning techniques. It has
demonstrated the applicability of ZPM synthesis
to direct and orient larger molecular
assemblies, such as nanoarchitectures,
into thin-film assemblies using molecular
structures with cross-sectional areas
larger than have been previously reported.
Furthermore, the squares were characterized
by X-ray reflectivity
